amountSemantics: modeled marginal donor expenditure, not a verified funding offer
scope: One additional summer placement; not school-year MYEEP or all JCYC programs

anchors.mortalityWindow: Cumulative through October 2014 for NYC 2005–08 cohorts; not annual
anchors.effectType: 2SLS participation effect; do not divide again by lottery take-up

judgments.label: Donor cost per additional summer slot
judgments.basis: 150 hours * $19.61 * 1.12 + $1,800 = $5,094.48, rounded to $5,100. Design hours and current posted wage are anchors; paying all training hours, 12% loading, $1,800 delivery allowance and transfer to a future summer cohort are assumptions, not a JCYC quote.

judgments.label: Share of external mortality effect retained
judgments.basis: 25% is a subjective allowance for different baseline risks, program design, geography, vintage and uncertain marginal participant mix. It is not an estimated SF effect.

judgments.label: Share of a funded slot that is additional
judgments.basis: 75% allows replacement of existing funding or another placement. No current unfunded cohort or private-gift allocation has been verified.

judgments.label: Discounted QALYs per death prevented
judgments.basis: 15 is a rounded judgment, not measured youth life expectancy. An illustrative 40-year horizon with utility 0.85, annual hazard 0.01, 3% discount and five-year delay gives about 14.7 QALYs. Mortality timing and long-run persistence remain unverified.

nullBoundary: No additional slots, no transferred mortality effect, or no lasting survival gain means zero additional QALYs and no finite price. Positive scenarios are not confidence intervals; adverse effects are not ruled out.

fundingRoom.nextEvidence: Summer-only incremental wage and delivery budget, unmet eligible demand, counterfactual placements and current private-gift capacity; no contact has been made.

excluded: Current earnings and household consumption gains
Education and longer-run earnings gains, which are not established by the selected experiment
Public-payer savings and broader societal value
